## Problem

This warm-up exercise has **two tasks**.

**Task A — Environment check.**
Run the code cell in Section 1 to confirm that your Python environment is
set up correctly for Exercises 8.1 and 8.2.

**Task B — Handout study with AI Tutor.**
Read Sections 4–5 of the shared Lectures 7–8 handout
(available at
[`nonlinear-equations-handout.html`](https://waseda-num-analysis-2026.github.io/materials/070/nonlinear-equations-handout.html))
and add **at least 3 Q&A blocks** using the AI Tutor workflow described in
Section 2 below.
The annotated handout lives in the `materials` repository — **you do not
need to copy it into this repository**.

AI is **recommended** for this exercise (the whole point is to interact
with the AI Tutor).

## 2. Handout Study with AI Tutor

### Goal

While reading the shared Lectures 7–8 handout, insert **at least 3 Q&A
blocks** of your own — questions you actually had while reading,
answered with the help of an AI (GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, etc.) following
the protocol in
[`AI_TUTOR.md`](https://github.com/waseda-num-analysis-2026/materials/blob/main/AI_TUTOR.md).

**Target:** focus on **Section 4** (multi-dimensional Newton's method) and
**Section 5** (simultaneous polynomial root-finding by the DK method),
which are the topics for Lecture 8 and Exercises 8.1–8.2.
Questions about any other section of the handout are also accepted.

### Steps

1. Open the handout file you cloned from the `materials` repository:
   `materials/070/nonlinear-equations-handout.qmd`
   (or the Japanese version `nonlinear-equations-handout-jp.qmd`).

2. **Prime the AI once per chat session.**
   Open `materials/AI_TUTOR.md`, press `Cmd+L` / `Ctrl+L`, and send:

   > Read this file.  From now on, follow these rules whenever I ask
   > about my handout.

3. **For each question:**
   - Highlight the line in the handout that confuses you.
   - Press `Cmd+L` / `Ctrl+L` and ask:

     > I don't understand this line.
     > Please add a Q&A block here following AI_TUTOR.md rules.

   - Read the AI's answer and verify it makes sense.
   - Accept the inserted Q&A block.

4. Repeat for **at least 3 distinct questions**.

5. Render the annotated handout to confirm the Q&A blocks are
   formatted correctly:

   ```bash
   cd materials/070
   quarto render nonlinear-equations-handout.qmd
   ```

   Open the generated `.html` file in your browser and check that the
   Q&A callout blocks appear.

> **Note:** You do **not** submit the annotated handout in this
> repository.  The Q&A blocks live inside `materials/070/nonlinear-equations-handout.qmd`,
> which is your personal evolving study note.
